scope: Google, Microsoft Learn, official learning repositories, foundational research and optional YouTube references. OpenAI researched separately.
method: Searched authoritative sources and opened written pages. Evidence is paraphrased. Paper entries are abstract-level verification. Video references are explicitly not content-verified.

sources.title: Beginner: Introduction to Generative AI
sources.page_evidence: Overview names LLM fundamentals and responsible AI; the catalog lists four activities.
sources.curriculum_use: Opening preparation; introductory level before model-building.
sources.limits: Catalog read; signed-in course activities were not completed.

sources.title: Introduction to generative AI and agents
sources.page_evidence: Learning objectives cover core GenAI concepts, how LLMs work, effective prompts, and agents.
sources.curriculum_use: Starting overview and vocabulary; not a complete MSc syllabus.
sources.limits: Module objectives and linked text units read.

sources.title: Introduction to Large Language Models
sources.page_evidence: Defines tokens and probability-based language modelling; objectives include context, parameters, self-attention and limitations.
sources.curriculum_use: LLM foundations; small probability and token examples.
sources.limits: Page read. Course prerequisites include ML and neural networks.

sources.title: Embeddings
sources.page_evidence: Contrasts sparse encoding with dense representations and gives similarity-based examples.
sources.curriculum_use: Explain vector similarity before document retrieval.
sources.limits: Page read; a hand-made vector example must be labelled illustrative, not a trained embedding.

sources.title: LLMs: Fine-tuning, distillation, and prompt engineering
sources.page_evidence: Explains task-specific training, parameter-efficient tuning, distillation, and prompting without changing model parameters.
sources.curriculum_use: Compare ways to adapt a model and establish a real small fine-tuning exercise.
sources.limits: Page read. Some broad claims are teaching simplifications; do not imply all tasks require fine-tuning or larger models always win.

sources.title: Prompt design strategies
sources.page_evidence: Sections cover specific instructions, response formats, examples, context, decomposition and iterative evaluation.
sources.curriculum_use: Prompt comparisons on a fixed task and rubric.
sources.limits: Page read. Model-specific parameter advice changes; do not teach universal temperature settings or guaranteed determinism.

sources.title: Structured outputs
sources.page_evidence: Introduces JSON Schema outputs; best practices require validating values and handling semantically incorrect results.
sources.curriculum_use: Separate format validity from factual correctness.
sources.limits: Page read. API schema subsets and model support must be rechecked before live delivery.

sources.title: Long context
sources.page_evidence: Describes context windows, multimodal inputs and limitations when retrieving several facts; notes latency and cost considerations.
sources.curriculum_use: Context selection and long-context versus retrieval trade-offs.
sources.limits: Page read. Do not generalize vendor benchmark or capacity figures to every model.

sources.title: Image understanding
sources.page_evidence: Describes image captioning, classification, visual Q&A, multiple image inputs and example API calls.
sources.curriculum_use: Image-to-text lab; distinguish visible evidence from interpretation.
sources.limits: Page read; API calls were not executed.

sources.title: Audio understanding
sources.page_evidence: Lists audio description, summarization, transcription, translation and timestamp-based analysis.
sources.curriculum_use: Short consented audio transcript comparison.
sources.limits: Page read; audio generation is a different capability. Do not treat emotion labels as reliable facts.

sources.title: Video understanding
sources.page_evidence: Describes video description, information extraction, Q&A and timestamp references.
sources.curriculum_use: Video evidence checking and temporal errors.
sources.limits: Page read; no videos were watched through this documentation.

sources.title: Grounding with Google Search
sources.page_evidence: Describes searching current web information and returning citations linked to response text.
sources.curriculum_use: Verify claims and citations; compare web grounding with course-document RAG.
sources.limits: Page read; availability and charges were not tested.

sources.title: Function calling with the Gemini API
sources.page_evidence: Workflow defines tools, sends declarations, obtains model-selected arguments, executes application code, then returns tool results.
sources.curriculum_use: Bounded calculator or read-only lookup demonstration.
sources.limits: Page read. The application executes the function; model-generated arguments are not authorization.

sources.title: Safety and factuality guidance
sources.page_evidence: Explains unexpected inaccurate or biased outputs, application-specific risk, iterative testing, prompt injection and human oversight.
sources.curriculum_use: Responsible practice throughout the course and a small failure-case test set.
sources.limits: Page read. This is application guidance, not legal advice or proof filters eliminate risk.

sources.title: Implement a responsible generative AI solution in Microsoft Foundry
sources.page_evidence: Objectives cover identifying, measuring and mitigating harms and responsible operation.
sources.curriculum_use: Use harm-identify-test-mitigate cycle in student evaluations.
sources.limits: Module objectives read. Product exercise requires prior Foundry familiarity; do not require it for the basic lab.

sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) evaluators
sources.page_evidence: Separates retrieval evaluation from answer groundedness, relevance and completeness.
sources.curriculum_use: Evaluate retrieval and generated answers separately using simple human labels.
sources.limits: Page read. LLM judges and provider metrics are examples, not ground truth or mandatory infrastructure.

sources.title: Getting started with customizing a large language model (LLM) (classic)
sources.page_evidence: Compares prompting, RAG and fine-tuning and says they can be complementary; recommends a baseline before tuning.
sources.curriculum_use: Decision exercise about missing knowledge versus inconsistent behaviour.
sources.limits: Page read, including classic-portal notice; use for concepts, not current UI steps.

sources.title: AI agents
sources.page_evidence: Explains model, instructions, knowledge tools and action tools; introduces multiple agents.
sources.curriculum_use: Basic workflow tracing; single agent before multi-agent awareness.
sources.limits: Text unit read; embedded video not watched.

sources.title: Generative AI for Beginners (Version 3)
sources.page_evidence: Repository distinguishes conceptual lessons from build lessons and links chapters on prompting, RAG, tools, agents and fine-tuning.
sources.curriculum_use: Supplementary reading and optional build references.
sources.limits: README read. External code was not run; product setup can change.

sources.title: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?
sources.page_evidence: Defines an open standard connecting AI applications with external data, tools and workflows.
sources.curriculum_use: Brief interoperability awareness; distinguish protocol from model and vector database.
sources.limits: Page read; URL redirects to versioned 2026-07-28 documentation. Protocol implementation is outside this overview.

sources.title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
sources.page_evidence: Abstract introduces latent-variable inference, reparameterization and variational lower-bound optimization.
sources.curriculum_use: Teacher reference for VAE fundamentals.
sources.limits: Abstract and bibliographic metadata read; not a full mathematical review.

sources.title: Generative Adversarial Networks
sources.page_evidence: Abstract defines a generator and discriminator trained through an adversarial objective.
sources.curriculum_use: Teacher reference for GAN comparison.
sources.limits: Abstract and bibliographic metadata read.

sources.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
sources.page_evidence: Abstract describes diffusion probabilistic image generation and its denoising connection.
sources.curriculum_use: Teacher reference for diffusion foundations.
sources.limits: Abstract and bibliographic metadata read; historical benchmark numbers are not current rankings.

sources.title: Attention Is All You Need
sources.page_evidence: Abstract introduces the attention-based Transformer architecture for sequence transduction.
sources.curriculum_use: Original Transformer reference and architecture history.
sources.limits: Abstract and bibliographic metadata read; original encoder-decoder design is not every modern LLM architecture.

sources.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
sources.page_evidence: Abstract describes freezing pretrained weights while learning low-rank matrices, reducing trainable parameter counts.
sources.curriculum_use: Explain real parameter-efficient adaptation with a small training experiment.
sources.limits: Abstract and metadata read. Do not claim benchmark savings apply to all hardware or all models.

sources.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
sources.page_evidence: Abstract identifies BERT as bidirectional encoder representations for language understanding.
sources.curriculum_use: Correct architecture comparison: BERT is not an autoregressive chat generator.
sources.limits: Abstract and bibliographic metadata read.

sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
sources.page_evidence: Abstract combines pretrained parametric knowledge with retrieved non-parametric memory for generation.
sources.curriculum_use: Historical RAG reference; explain external evidence supporting generation.
sources.limits: Abstract and bibliographic metadata read. The original trained RAG system differs from a simple classroom pipeline.
